title_i18n.en: The npm of the AI agent world is here! Vercel launches Skills.sh, aiming to unify agent instruction sets.
title_i18n.es: ¡Llega el npm del mundo de los agentes de IA! Vercel lanza Skills.sh, con el objetivo de unificar los conjuntos de instrucciones para agentes inteligentes.

excerpt_i18n.zh: Vercel 最近发布了开源项目 Skills.sh ，想要给 AI 智能体（Agents）配上一套“标准动作库”。简单来说，它让智能体能通过命令行执行各种可复用的操作，也就是所谓的“技能”（Skills）。Vercel 将其定义为一个 开放的智能体技能生态系统 ，开发者可以在这里定义、分享并运行一个个独立的指令，供智能体在工作流中随时调用。这一工具的核心逻辑，是把智能体的“推理”和“执行”分开——让智能体去调用那些受控、预定义的命令，而不是由它自己去瞎猜、乱写 shell 逻辑。
excerpt_i18n.en: Vercel recently launched the open-source project Skills.sh, aiming to equip AI agents with a "standard action library." Essentially, it enables agents to execute various reusable operations via the command line, known as "Skills." Vercel defines it as an open ecosystem for agent skills, where developers can define, share, and run individual commands for agents to invoke as needed within workflows. The core logic of this tool is to separate an agent's "reasoning" from its "execution"—allowing agents to call controlled, predefined commands instead of having them guess or write shell logic haphazardly on their own.
excerpt_i18n.es: Vercel ha lanzado recientemente el proyecto de código abierto Skills.sh, con el objetivo de dotar a los agentes de IA de una "biblioteca de acciones estándar". En esencia, permite que los agentes ejecuten diversas operaciones reutilizables a través de la línea de comandos, conocidas como "habilidades" (Skills). Vercel lo define como un ecosistema abierto de habilidades para agentes, donde los desarrolladores pueden definir, compartir y ejecutar instrucciones independientes para que los agentes las utilicen en sus flujos de trabajo cuando sea necesario. La lógica central de esta herramienta es separar el "razonamiento" del "ejecución" de los agentes, permitiéndoles invocar comandos controlados y predefinidos.

items.title: Empusa – Visual debugger to catch and resume AI agent retry loops
items.raw_excerpt: OP here. I’ve been running autonomous agents (OpenClaw/ReplyX) for lead gen, and I kept waking up to drained API credits because bots would get stuck in "zombie loops"—retrying a failed step (like a button click) until the timeout hit. I actually wrote the fix for the loop detection logic in the OpenClaw repo itself (PR #9759), but I realized I needed a better way to visualize what was happening than scrolling through thousands of lines of JSON logs. Empusa is a local dashboard (Next.js + SQLite) that helps with this: Visual Timeline: Turns logs into a visual trace (Green=Success, Red=Fail, Yellow=Loop Detected). State Snapshots: It records the agent's variable state at every step. Resume Capability: If an agent crashes, you can grab the state JSON and resume execution from that exact step

items.title: OpenAI首款硬件命名曝光，有望今年发售
items.raw_excerpt: 博主@智慧皮卡丘 今天（2 月 7 日）在 X 平台发布推文，透露 OpenAI 的首款硬件名为 Dime（直译为 10 美分），是一款类似苹果 AirPods 的耳机产品。 在发展战略方面，消息源透露 OpenAI 搁置此前爆料的激进方案，该公司原本计划打造一款“类手机”架构的革命性设备，其内部堆料豪华，不仅拥有独立的算力，物料成本（BOM）甚至媲美智能手机。而 OpenAI 目前倾向于“先易后难”，优先开发一款功能相对单一、更接近传统形态的 AI 音频耳机。 促成这一战略急转弯的核心原因，在于居高不下的硬件成本。爆料指出，当前存储芯片供应短缺，导致组件价格飙升，导致打造一款“高算力耳机”的成本变得难以取得合理商业回报。 基于当前的供应链环境，OpenAI 重新规划了发布时间表。报告显示，这款代号为 Dime 的基础版 AI 耳机有望在 2026 年推向市场。公司计划先通过这款门槛较低的产品在硬件领域站稳脚跟，积累用户数据与市场反馈。（新浪财经）

Blogger @SmartPikachu posted on X today (February 7), revealing that OpenAI's first hardware product is named Dime (literally translated as 10 cents), a headphone device similar to Apple's AirPods. Regarding development strategy, sources disclosed that OpenAI has shelved the previously reported aggressive plan. The company originally intended to create a revolutionary "phone-like" architecture device with high-end internal components, featuring independent computing power and a bill of materials (BOM) cost comparable to that of a smartphone. OpenAI now leans toward an "easier first, harder later" approach, prioritizing the development of an AI audio headphone with relatively single functionality and a more traditional form factor.

The core reason for this strategic shift lies in the persistently high hardware costs. The report points out that the current shortage of memory chip supply has led to soaring component prices, making it difficult to achieve reasonable commercial returns from producing a "high-computing headphone."

Based on the current supply chain environment, OpenAI has revised its release timeline. Reports indicate that this basic AI headphone, codenamed Dime, is expected to hit the market in 2026. The company plans to establish a foothold in the hardware sector with this lower-barrier product first, accumulating user data and market feedback. (Sina Finance)

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past decade, TypeScript has been regarded by many teams as the solution for "engineering JavaScript." In the era of AI programming, it has unexpectedly become one of the most convenient languages for AI. The reason is simple: AI's ability to write code largely depends on how much code in that language it has been exposed to, and TypeScript/JavaScript happens to be among the languages with the richest training data. More importantly, TypeScript explicitly includes semantic cues like types and interfaces in the code, making it easier for AI to understand, refactor, and complete.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la última década, TypeScript ha sido considerado por muchos equipos como la respuesta a la "ingeniería de JavaScript"; en la era de la programación con IA, sorprendentemente se ha convertido en uno de los lenguajes más manejables para la IA. La razón es simple: la capacidad de la IA para escribir código depende básicamente de cuánto código en ese lenguaje haya visto, y TypeScript/JavaScript resulta ser uno de los que tiene el corpus de entrenamiento más abundante. Lo más crucial es que TypeScript incluye explícitamente en el código "pistas semánticas" como tipos e interfaces, lo que facilita que la IA comprenda, refactorice y complete el código.

items.title: 清华刘知远团队论文：最小化结构改动，短文本到长文本丝滑升级 | ICLR 2026

excerpt_i18n.en: In the rapid advancement of large language models toward stronger reasoning capabilities and more complex application scenarios, "context length" has evolved from a model configuration parameter into a critical bottleneck limiting the upper bound of system capabilities. On one hand, tasks such as long document comprehension, cross-turn dialogue memory, complex planning, and long-chain reasoning demand far beyond the traditional 4k or 8k sequence lengths. On the other hand, the computational pattern based on full attention mechanisms in mainstream Transformer architectures inevitably leads to quadratic increases in time and memory costs as sequence length grows, making "supporting longer contexts" quickly translate into prohibitive costs in practical engineering. Amid this contradiction, sparse attention has almost become a consensus direction in both academia and industry, yet it has not led to a complete solution but rather a series of new structural tensions. Over the past few years, numerous efforts have attempted to alleviate computational pressure by introducing new attention structures, routing mechanisms, or trainable sparse modules. While these methods often excel in theoretical complexity or specific benchmarks, they have gradually revealed a long-underestimated issue in real-world model training and deployment workflows: current large language models almost universally follow the training paradigm of "short-sequence pre-training, long-sequence fine-tuning," and some sparse attention solutions that modify model architecture, such as NSA, exhibit significant misalignment with standard dense attention in structure, parameters, or output format. items.title: 当 AI 开始写 80% 的代码，架构才是真正的护城河

excerpt_i18n.en: GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke recently issued a stern warning: "Embrace AI or leave the profession." However, embracing AI is not just about using code autocompletion tools. It signifies a shift in our core competencies—from mastering syntax to systems thinking, learning to break down problems until they are small enough for AI to solve. In short, we are all architects now.
excerpt_i18n.es: El CEO de GitHub, Thomas Dohmke, recientemente emitió una severa advertencia: "Adopta la IA o abandona la profesión". Significa un cambio en nuestras capacidades fundamentales: pasar del dominio de la sintaxis al pensamiento sistémico, aprendiendo a descomponer problemas hasta que sean lo suficientemente pequeños para que la IA los resuelva. En resumen: ahora todos somos arquitectos.
